research.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are fighting for the open seat of retiring Sen. Gary Peters, with Newsweek reporting most October polls showing El-Sayed narrowly ahead and Cook and Sabato rating it a toss up. Republicans have outspent Democrats with ads casting El-Sayed as too extreme on policing, immigration and health care, while El-Sayed ties Rogers to Trump, the Iran war and AIPAC money.

issues.why: El-Sayed backs Medicare for All with guaranteed coverage, while Rogers says it would strip private insurance and proposes expanding TrumpRx drug pricing.
El-Sayed says Rogers backs an aimless war voters pay for at the pump, while Rogers says El-Sayed will not condemn the IRGC.
Rogers backs tariffs that work for Michigan, wants to wrap up the Canada dispute and keep Chinese automakers out, while El-Sayed favors targeted tariffs.
El-Sayed wants to abolish ICE, which Republicans feature in attack ads, while Rogers defends Trump's immigration strategy.
Rogers says he would back a one year moratorium on new data centers, while El-Sayed wants AI firms regulated like utilities.

storylines.title: Obama and Democratic stars rally for El-Sayed
storylines.what: Obama was scheduled to campaign with El-Sayed in Detroit to bank early votes, after Kamala Harris held a roundtable with him, as he works to shore up Black voters who favored Haley Stevens in the primary.

storylines.title: Final debate turns fiery
storylines.what: In the second and final debate El-Sayed attacked Rogers over the Iran war and Trump, while Rogers raised El-Sayed's past defund the police posts and the cost of Medicare for All.

storylines.title: Rogers presses on IRGC and ideology
storylines.what: Rogers said El-Sayed cannot condemn the IRGC and his campaign renewed claims tying El-Sayed donors to the Muslim Brotherhood, which El-Sayed denies and calls shameful.

storylines.title: Marist shows El-Sayed up two
storylines.what: A Marist poll of likely voters had El-Sayed at 50 percent and Rogers at 48, while a Rogers aligned poll showed Rogers ahead by two.

storylines.title: Republicans make El-Sayed the target
storylines.what: Republicans outspent Democrats 78 million to 63 million on ads calling El-Sayed dangerously radical, and Trump and Vance attacked him personally. El-Sayed says he is not shying away from the fight.

storylines.title: AIPAC super PAC mails against El-Sayed
storylines.what: The United Democracy Project spent about 95,000 dollars on mail to Jewish voters attacking El-Sayed over a remark he later apologized for, after Rogers said he would take any help.

storylines.title: Grand Rapids debate
storylines.what: The candidates met in a televised debate at WOOD TV in Grand Rapids, their first of two.

events.title: Medicare for All question
events.prompt: Attack ads say single payer health care would take away private insurance from millions of Michiganders. You are asked to state your health plan.

opts.label: Defend Medicare for All
opts.say: Make the case for guaranteed coverage for all, with union plans as a supplement.

opts.label: Expand the ACA
opts.say: Extend premium tax credits and add a public option instead of single payer.

opts.label: Price transparency
opts.say: Expand TrumpRx and penalize insurers that hide prices or deny care unfairly.

events.title: Iran war and gas prices
events.prompt: Gas and grocery prices are up and voters connect them to the war with Iran. A debate moderator asks whether you support the war.

opts.label: Oppose the war
opts.say: Call the war aimless and say tax dollars should be spent at home.

opts.label: Seek a quick end
opts.say: Say Iran is a threat but Congress must press for a fast resolution.

opts.label: Back the mission
opts.say: Support the administration and demand the other side condemn the IRGC.

events.title: Auto tariffs
events.prompt: Michigan automakers and suppliers are caught in tariff fights with Canada and competition from China. You must lay out a trade position.

opts.label: Targeted, pro worker
opts.say: Use targeted tariffs tied to union jobs and end corporate tax breaks for offshoring.

opts.label: End Canada fight
opts.say: Keep China out of US auto production but wrap up the tariff dispute with Canada.

opts.label: Full tariff push
opts.say: Back the president's tariffs as leverage to bring auto jobs home.

events.title: ICE and immigration
events.prompt: Republican ads highlight a call to abolish ICE. Voters in Macomb and Oakland ask what you would do on immigration enforcement.

opts.label: Abolish ICE
opts.say: Replace ICE, which you call a paramilitary force, with a new enforcement system.

opts.label: Reform enforcement
opts.say: Keep enforcement but add oversight and focus on serious criminals.

opts.label: Back Trump's approach
opts.say: Defend the administration's strategy as a former FBI agent focused on security.
